summary.oneLiner: Integrated dairy company owning the value chain from the farmer's collection point to the consumer's table, across South India, Western India, Eastern India and East Africa.
summary.business: Dodla Dairy procures milk directly from farmers across eight states through a network of village-level collection and chilling centres, and processes it into fresh liquid milk, curd and a widening portfolio of value-added products (paneer, cheese, ghee, ice cream, UHT milk, flavoured milk, yoghurt, buttermilk and lassi) sold under its own brands. The integrated model extends beyond its Southern India home markets into Eastern India (via the OSAM acquisition in Bihar/Jharkhand) and into East Africa (Uganda and Kenya), with Orgafeed supplying cattle feed to strengthen farmer productivity.

currentContext.strengths: Fully integrated value chain from direct farmer procurement (approximately 1.3 lakh farmer partners across 10,970+ villages) through processing to branded retail distribution|Deep multi-channel distribution reach: 17 sales offices, 110+ agents, 3,210+ distributors, 2,880+ retail parlours, 1,106 exclusive outlets and 8,000+ village-level collection/chilling centres|Geographic diversification across Southern, Western and Eastern India plus East Africa (Uganda and Kenya), reducing dependence on any single procurement or demand region|Direct-from-farmer procurement model (predominantly cow milk, ~95% of sourcing) providing granular visibility over supply volumes, quality and procurement pricing|Net-debt-free balance sheet with INR 659.4 crores of cash and liquid investments, enabling capex to be funded entirely through internal accruals|Widening value-added product portfolio (curd, paneer, ghee, ice cream, flavoured milk) supporting margin mix shift away from low-margin bulk SMP/butter
currentContext.strategies: Deepen procurement, improve value-added product contribution, strengthen OSAM, progress the Maharashtra project, scale East Africa with discipline, and continue investing in quality and brand trust.|Standard operating practice of being a net seller of milk solids, converting milk into solids when conditions are favourable and holding inventory with discipline to support product availability and margin management during tighter periods.|Expand production capacity by widening the regionally distributed production network to reduce regional dependency, lower logistics costs and serve high-potential markets faster.|Deepen the direct procurement model across states through a decentralised model that spreads risk, cushions seasonal shifts and secures milk at competitive rates.|Focus on value-added products (VAPs) as the engine of profitability, aligning product development with local tastes given their superior margin profile and brand-building potential.|Strengthen the brand and expand reach across India and Africa, including growth in quick commerce and e-commerce with a focus on freshness, temperature control and fulfilment discipline.|Scale East Africa (Uganda and Kenya) as a measured growth geography through deliberate market selection, pricing discipline and continued direct farmer engagement, rather than as an open-ended commitment.|Embed technology across the procurement-to-consumer chain (real-time fat/SNF testing via GPRS-enabled analysers, SAP-enabled procurement and payments, automated processing, digitised traceability) to scale operating control without proportional cost increase.|Use Orgafeed as a supply-side lever, supplying quality cattle feed through the procurement network and adjusting value against milk supplied to improve farmer productivity, retention and supply reliability.|Dividend is recommended annually by the Board (final dividend of INR 5 per equity share for FY 2025-26, i.e. 50% of face value) and is payable out of the Company's profits subject to shareholder approval at the AGM. The Company also extends financial support to its subsidiaries, including a corporate guarantee to wholly owned subsidiary Orgafeed Private Limited to help it access bank financing for working capital and capital expenditure requirements.
currentContext.expansion: The Company's principal ongoing capacity project is a greenfield integrated dairy plant near Solapur, Maharashtra, with a planned processing capacity of 10 LLPD and a planned total capex of INR 2,800 million; civil work is underway, INR 1,060 million had been deployed as of 31 March 2026, and commercial operations are targeted by the end of 2026-27, with an initial focus on SMP and butter before expanding into value-added products. Alongside the dairy plant, the Company is establishing a greenfield cattle-feed manufacturing plant in Maharashtra to support the growing procurement/farmer base in the region. In Eastern India, the Company acquired HR Food Processing Private Limited (OSAM) in August 2025 for INR 2,472 million, adding two operational processing plants (Arrah, Bihar and Patratu, Jharkhand) with combined capacity of ~2.2 LLPD and a distribution network across 42 districts; a further 7-acre land parcel has been allotted by BIADA for an OSAM dairy project, requiring an additional INR 44 million investment. In East Africa, the Company secured a ~70-acre land parcel roughly 100 km from Kampala, Uganda, for a greenfield expansion with a planned total investment of INR 600 million over two years (INR 44 million invested in 2025-26), targeting the fresh/pasteurised milk segment and an expanded yogurt operation, with planned capacity addition of ~2 LLPD; the project is being executed in two phases (Phase 1: flavoured yoghurt, toned/skim/full-cream milk, paneer, cheese, ghee and packaged drinking water; Phase 2: long-life milk, ice cream and milk powder) and is expected to commence revenue generation by the end of FY 2028-29.
currentContext.mdna: Milk supply availability is expected to improve and input costs to normalise gradually into 2026-27, which should support a gradual recovery in gross margin.|Full-year contribution of the OSAM acquisition, continued momentum in Africa, and organic growth in India are expected to support the operating plan for 2026-27.|2025-26 was marked by industry-wide tightness in milk supply that kept procurement costs firm through months that ordinarily bring seasonal easing.|The dairy sector is shifting steadily from unorganised to organised channels, driven by food safety regulation, rising consumer preference for branded products, and growing demand from institutional and export markets requiring quality and traceability.|Dairy consumption is shifting toward branded and value-added products, driven by urbanisation, rising incomes and health awareness, with demand growing across nutrition, protein, probiotic formats, bakery applications and out-of-home consumption.|Dairy distribution is expanding across modern retail, quick commerce, institutional channels and export markets, requiring strong branding, consistent quality and cold-chain capability.|Selling price actions during 2025-26 were taken selectively and in line with demand-supply conditions, competitive intensity and category seasonality, to protect the consumer franchise while avoiding decisions that could weaken long-term market position.

risks.note: Inflation, exchange-rate fluctuations and changes in consumer purchasing power can affect profitability; milk procurement costs are particularly sensitive during lean seasons, and price increases cannot always be passed through in full without risking market share.

risks.risk: Supply chain / raw milk procurement risk
risks.note: Operations depend heavily on a stable supply of raw milk, packaging materials and other inputs; disruptions to milk supply (e.g. from erratic rainfall shortening the flush season) can directly affect production and cost of procurement.
The dairy industry is highly competitive with both organised and unorganised players offering similar products, creating pressure on pricing and market share.

Risks to the Company's strategic positioning and execution choices — including raising the VAP contribution to revenue, forming e-commerce partnerships, and expanding into new geographies — could disrupt the core assumptions of its business strategy if not managed well.

Potential fines, litigation costs and enforcement actions can arise from changes in legal and regulatory requirements, conflicts of interest, or compliance breaches, given operations span multiple states and countries (India, Uganda, Kenya).

Maintaining product quality and safety is critical to customer trust and regulatory compliance; any lapse could severely impact reputation given the Company's scale and multi-state, multi-country distribution.

Increasing reliance on technology across procurement, processing and distribution (digitised procurement, GPRS-enabled analysers, SAP systems) creates exposure to system failure or cyberattack that could impact operational efficiency and data security.
Consumer preferences in dairy can shift rapidly; failure to anticipate and adapt product mix and formats could erode the Company's market share and first-mover advantage.

one-line thesis: Dodla Dairy delivered record Q4 revenue (+18% YoY) driven by volume growth and Africa expansion, but EBITDA margins compressed to 5% due to elevated milk procurement costs and packaging inflation. Reported PAT was artificially inflated by INR 39 crores in tax reversals, masking an underlying profitability dip that management expects to normalize in FY27 as supply improves.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 1,074 cr (+18% YoY); EBITDA: INR 54 cr (5% margin vs ~7-8% historical); PAT (Reported): INR 70 cr (+66% YoY) includes INR 29 cr tax reversal + INR 10 cr interest income; PAT (Normalized): ~INR 40 cr (-52% YoY underlying); Order Book: N/A (FMCG); Net Debt: Near zero (D/E 0.03), Cash INR 649 cr.
guidance: Revenue growth: Low-to-mid teens for FY27; Margin: 50-100 bps recovery over FY26 levels (targeting ~8-8.5%); Order Inflow: N/A; Capex: INR 130 cr standalone + INR 180 cr for Maharashtra project in FY27.
order book & pipeline: N/A for FMCG; Procurement stable at 18.5 LLPD (+13.4% YoY); Africa milk sales volume +60% YoY.
segment / subsidiary detail: India Liquid Milk: 14 LLPD sales, realization INR 58.4/L; VAP: INR 297 cr (+21% ex-bulk), Curd +15.4%; Africa: Revenue INR 151 cr (+48% YoY), EBITDA INR 18 cr (record); OrgaFeed: Revenue +23.2%, margins dipped due to raw material/freight; OSAM: Revenue INR 82 cr, EBITDA INR 2.7 cr (margins ~3.3%, targeting convergence to 25% gross).
growth verticals / optionality: Maharashtra greenfield (commercial ops by FY27 end); Uganda Phase 2 expansion (INR 60 cr capex, completion FY29); Bihar project (7 acres allocated, INR 4.4 cr land cost, under board consideration); Africa target 15-18% of consolidated revenue by FY28.
margins & cost dynamics: Milk procurement cost rose to INR 41/L (from INR 37.4/L YoY); Packaging costs up 30%; Freight pressure due to diesel prices; Only INR 1/L of inflation passed on to consumers in Q4; Management expects procurement cost to drop by ~INR 1/L in late May.
capex / expansion: FY26 Total: INR 430 cr (INR 271 cr HR Food/Africa, INR 86 cr Maharashtra, INR 73 cr maintenance); FY27 Plan: INR 130 cr standalone regular + INR 180 cr for Maharashtra balance (of INR 280 cr total project); Uganda: INR 60 cr budgeted over phases till FY29.
capital allocation: Priority 1: Fund growth capex (Maharashtra, Uganda) via internal accruals; Priority 2: Regular dividends (INR 5/share final); Priority 3: Selective bolt-on acquisitions for procurement/distribution synergies.
risks & watch-items: El Niño/weather impact on fodder and milk yields; Persistent fuel/packaging inflation (plastics +30%); Delay in milk supply normalization; Execution risk on Maharashtra/Uganda expansions; OSAM margin convergence delays.
management quality / tone: Cautiously optimistic; Emphasizes 'caution' regarding external uncertainties (fuel, urea, weather) while affirming long-term volume growth; Transparent about one-offs distorting PAT.
non-obvious takeaways: Reported PAT surge is entirely non-operational (tax refunds); Underlying business profitability halved YoY; Management explicitly avoiding grammage reduction to preserve consumer trust, opting for small price hikes instead; OSAM acquisition dragging consolidated margins temporarily but expected to converge in 6-12 months.

| High milk procurement costs and packaging inflation compressing margins for pure-play dairy peers without diversified feed or international exposure. | Dodla Dairy Limited | beneficiary | Med | While margins are compressed, Dodla's Africa growth (+48%) and OrgaFeed vertical provide a hedge that pure-play Indian dairy competitors lack; normalized PAT base of INR 215 cr offers a clean entry point if supply normalizes. |
| Rising input costs and potential volume slowdown due to inflation. | Regional Dairy Cooperatives | loser | Low | Cooperatives are following Dodla's price hikes (INR 2), suggesting industry-wide margin pressure; lack of agile VAP mix or international diversification may hurt them more in a prolonged inflationary cycle. |

themes.title: Consumption revival & FMCG premiumization
themes.need: Rural recovery, GST 2.0 and premiumization still frame the theme, but Q1FY27 rewarded portfolio SHAPE over volume. TATACONSUM's growth businesses hit INR 1,300cr (+47%) and are now 36% of India - larger than either salt (>INR 1,000cr) or tea & coffee (INR 1,200cr), with Sampann +58%, RTD +41% and Capital Foods INR 232cr (+40%) - while India tea revenue fell 4% on +2% volume as lower tea costs were deliberately passed back (tea inflation is now running 7-10% with most buying still ahead, so that inverts next year). PGHH shows the margin route: FY26 sales roughly flat at ~INR 4,300cr but PAT +19% to ~INR 850cr and ~100bps of structural margin from INR 86cr of productivity savings, absorbing crude and resin each up 30-50% with no stock-outs. The cautionary tale is licensed brands - JYOTHYLAB lost the Pril and Fa licences when Henkel did not renew (all manufacturing and selling stopped 1-June; Pril was ~7-8% of revenue, ~INR 225-240cr) and has filed SIAC arbitration. MARICO/DABUR/GODREJCP/COLPAL/EMAMILTD ride distribution + premium mix; VBL on beverage route-to-market; BIKAJI/GOPAL/BECTORFOOD on branded snacks; ORKLAINDIA took a 4% blended price increase in Q4 plus premium mix to a 16.9% EBITDA margin.
themes.driver: GST 2.0 demand pull-through; rural volume recovery; festive/wedding restocking; commodity pass-back timing; JYOTHYLAB's ~7-8% revenue hole and the SIAC arbitration.

themes.title: Agri value-chain - food processing, dairy, protein & seeds
themes.need: Rising protein/processed-food consumption, animal-nutrition demand and export tailwinds drive an integrated agri value-chain - DODLA/PARAGMILK on dairy; AVANTIFEED/SHINDL/SKMEGGPROD/HMAAGRO on aqua/poultry/meat protein; GODREJAGRO/KSCL/NATHBIOGEN on feed + seeds; REGAAL/SUKHJITS/GULPOLY on maize/starch; FOODSIN/MANORAMA on agri-processing & specialty fats.
themes.driver: Monsoon-led farm income; protein export demand; feed-margin recovery; festive processed-food restocking.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Dodla Dairy procures milk directly from farmers across eight states through a network of village-level collection and chilling centres, and processes it into fresh liquid milk, curd and a widening portfolio of value-added products (paneer, cheese, ghee, ice cream, UHT milk, flavoured milk, yoghurt, buttermilk and lassi) sold under its own brands. The integrated model extends beyond its Southern India home markets into Eastern India (via the OSAM acquisition in Bihar/Jharkhand) and into East Africa (Uganda and Kenya), with Orgafeed supplying cattle feed to strengthen farmer productivity.

group_structure.body:
- Orgafeed Private Limited — subsidiary: Wholly owned subsidiary (India); cattle feed manufacturing business supplying the Company's farmer procurement network.
- HR Food Processing Private Limited (OSAM) — subsidiary: Wholly owned subsidiary (India), acquired with effect from 01 August 2025; regional dairy brand extending the Company's presence into Eastern India.
- Dodla Holdings Pte. Limited — subsidiary: Wholly owned subsidiary (Singapore); holding company for the Company's East Africa operations.
- Country Delight Dairy Limited — subsidiary: Wholly owned subsidiary (Kenya).

- Lakeside Dairy Limited — subsidiary: Step-down subsidiary (Uganda), held through Dodla Holdings Pte. Limited.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Milk supply availability is expected to improve and input costs to normalise gradually into 2026-27, which should support a gradual recovery in gross margin.
- Full-year contribution of the OSAM acquisition, continued momentum in Africa, and organic growth in India are expected to support the operating plan for 2026-27.
- 2025-26 was marked by industry-wide tightness in milk supply that kept procurement costs firm through months that ordinarily bring seasonal easing.
- The dairy sector is shifting steadily from unorganised to organised channels, driven by food safety regulation, rising consumer preference for branded products, and growing demand from institutional and export markets requiring quality and traceability.
- Dairy consumption is shifting toward branded and value-added products, driven by urbanisation, rising incomes and health awareness, with demand growing across nutrition, protein, probiotic formats, bakery applications and out-of-home consumption.
- Dairy distribution is expanding across modern retail, quick commerce, institutional channels and export markets, requiring strong branding, consistent quality and cold-chain capability.
- Selling price actions during 2025-26 were taken selectively and in line with demand-supply conditions, competitive intensity and category seasonality, to protect the consumer franchise while avoiding decisions that could weaken long-term market position.

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Milk procurement cost rose to INR 41/L (from INR 37.4/L YoY); Packaging costs up 30%; Freight pressure due to diesel prices; Only INR 1/L of inflation passed on to consumers in Q4; Management expects procurement cost to drop by ~INR 1/L in late May.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Priority 1: Fund growth capex (Maharashtra, Uganda) via internal accruals; Priority 2: Regular dividends (INR 5/share final); Priority 3: Selective bolt-on acquisitions for procurement/distribution synergies.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The Company's principal ongoing capacity project is a greenfield integrated dairy plant near Solapur, Maharashtra, with a planned processing capacity of 10 LLPD and a planned total capex of INR 2,800 million; civil work is underway, INR 1,060 million had been deployed as of 31 March 2026, and commercial operations are targeted by the end of 2026-27, with an initial focus on SMP and butter before expanding into value-added products. Alongside the dairy plant, the Company is establishing a greenfield cattle-feed manufacturing plant in Maharashtra to support the growing procurement/farmer base in the region. In Eastern India, the Company acquired HR Food Processing Private Limited (OSAM) in August 2025 for INR 2,472 million, adding two operational processing plants (Arrah, Bihar and Patratu, Jharkhand) with combined capacity of ~2.2 LLPD and a distribution network across 42 districts; a further 7-acre land parcel has been allotted by BIADA for an OSAM dairy project, requiring an additional INR 44 million investment. In East Africa, the Company secured a ~70-acre land parcel roughly 100 km from Kampala, Uganda, for a greenfield expansion with a planned total investment of INR 600 million over two years (INR 44 million invested in 2025-26), targeting the fresh/pasteurised milk segment and an expanded yogurt operation, with planned capacity addition of ~2 LLPD; the project is being executed in two phases (Phase 1: flavoured yoghurt, toned/skim/full-cream milk, paneer, cheese, ghee and packaged drinking water; Phase 2: long-life milk, ice cream and milk powder) and is expected to commence revenue generation by the end of FY 2028-29.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Cautiously optimistic; Emphasizes 'caution' regarding external uncertainties (fuel, urea, weather) while affirming long-term volume growth; Transparent about one-offs distorting PAT.

litigation.title: Litigation & compliance (profile)
litigation.body: {"material": false, "note": "Standalone financial statement notes (Note 40, Contingent Liabilities) disclose claims against the Company not acknowledged as debts relating to income-tax matters and indirect tax matters on customs assessment of imported machinery, plus corporate guarantees outstanding; no operational or reputational litigation narrative is disclosed in the routed text.", "as_of": "2026-06-20"}

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Fully integrated value chain from direct farmer procurement (approximately 1.3 lakh farmer partners across 10,970+ villages) through processing to branded retail distribution
- Deep multi-channel distribution reach: 17 sales offices, 110+ agents, 3,210+ distributors, 2,880+ retail parlours, 1,106 exclusive outlets and 8,000+ village-level collection/chilling centres
- Geographic diversification across Southern, Western and Eastern India plus East Africa (Uganda and Kenya), reducing dependence on any single procurement or demand region
- Direct-from-farmer procurement model (predominantly cow milk, ~95% of sourcing) providing granular visibility over supply volumes, quality and procurement pricing
- Net-debt-free balance sheet with INR 659.4 crores of cash and liquid investments, enabling capex to be funded entirely through internal accruals
- Widening value-added product portfolio (curd, paneer, ghee, ice cream, flavoured milk) supporting margin mix shift away from low-margin bulk SMP/butter

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: El Niño/weather impact on fodder and milk yields; Persistent fuel/packaging inflation (plastics +30%); Delay in milk supply normalization; Execution risk on Maharashtra/Uganda expansions; OSAM margin convergence delays.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Reported PAT surge is entirely non-operational (tax refunds); Underlying business profitability halved YoY; Management explicitly avoiding grammage reduction to preserve consumer trust, opting for small price hikes instead; OSAM acquisition dragging consolidated margins temporarily but expected to converge in 6-12 months.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Deepen procurement, improve value-added product contribution, strengthen OSAM, progress the Maharashtra project, scale East Africa with discipline, and continue investing in quality and brand trust.
- Standard operating practice of being a net seller of milk solids, converting milk into solids when conditions are favourable and holding inventory with discipline to support product availability and margin management during tighter periods.
- Expand production capacity by widening the regionally distributed production network to reduce regional dependency, lower logistics costs and serve …

challenges.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers
challenges.body:

|---|---|---|---|---|
| High milk procurement costs and packaging inflation compressing margins for pure-play dairy peers without diversified feed or international exposure. | Dodla Dairy Limited | beneficiary | Med | While margins are compressed, Dodla's Africa growth (+48%) and OrgaFeed vertical provide a hedge that pure-play Indian dairy competitors lack; normalized PAT base of INR 215 cr offers a clean entry point if supply normalizes. |

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Acquisition] The deck gives two different dates for the same OSAM transaction: the expansion slide says "Acquired OSAM Dairy in Jul'26 for Rs. 247.2 Cr", while the OSAM snapshot says "Acquired HR Food Processing Private Limited (OSAM) in August 2025 for Rs 2,472 million" and the corporate-structure footnote says "The Company acquired HR Food Processing Private Limited (OSAM) with effect from 01 August 2025"; FY26 subsidiary financials are noted as "acquisition date onwards (Date - Aug 2025)".
- [Structure] Group holdings: Orgafeed Private Limited (India) 100%, HR Food Processing Private Limited (India) 100%, Dodla Holdings Proprietary Limited (Singapore) 100%, Country Delight Dairy Limited (Kenya) 100%, Dodla Dairy Kenya Limited (Kenya) 99%, Lakeside Dairy Limited (Uganda) 100%, and Global Vetmed Concepts India Private Limited (India) 47.88%.
- [Ownership] Shareholding as on 30th June 2026: Promoter 59%, Mutual Funds 24%, FIIs & Foreign Companies 6%, Non Institutional 11%, with 33,500+ total shareholders; key investors include SBI Mutual Funds 8.54%, HDFC Small Cap Fund 7.77%, DSP Small Cap Fund 6.60%, Bharat Biotech International Ltd 3.36%, B V K Reddy 1.63% and Steinberg India Emerging Opportunities Fund 1.33% (% of total equity).
- [Governance] Board includes Akshay Tanna, Partner and Head at KKR India Private Equity, as Non-Executive Non-Independent Director; the shareholder history runs from Black River (erstwhile name of PE fund Proterra) to The Rise Fund (TPG), with IFC investing ~INR 100 Cr around the 2021 BSE & NSE listing.
- [Restatement] The deck flags that "A minor revision has been made to Curd sales and VAP sales numbers for FY26 pursuant to the calibration of volume-related data."
- [Team] 4,000+ total head count, 450+ professionals, 30+ years average management experience, 6+ years average employee experience and 35 years average employee age.
